recipe.title: Buttered Toast
recipe.description: Thick bread is toasted crisp and buttered on both faces while hot, leaving a crunchy surface and a tender middle.

ingredients.name: bread, each about 19 mm (¾ inch) thick
ingredients.substitution: Use the same number of similarly sized wheat, white or sourdough slices. Gluten-free bread may toast faster.

ingredients.name: softened salted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a spreadable dairy-free butter alternative; flavor and browning differ.

steps: Arrange {{bread}} on a rack over a baking tray. Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toast for about 6–10 minutes, turning halfway, until both faces are crisp and golden. Watch the final minutes closely.
Spread {{butter|0.5}} over one face of the warm slices. Turn them over and spread the remaining {{butter|0.5}} over the other face.
Serve two slices per person immediately. For a larger batch, toast in uncrowded batches; do not multiply the oven temperature or per-batch time.
recipe.notes: The source specified bread thickness and buttering both sides but no quantities. This adaptation sets four slices, 28 g butter and an oven method. Bread size changes the portion size. Yield and timing are planning estimates. This adaptation has not been kitchen-tested.
recipe.source: The English and Australian Cookery Book (1864), Edward Abbott. https://archive.org/details/b21505524 Modern adaptation by SavorShelf.

recipe.title: Mashed Potatoes
recipe.description: Steamed potatoes are mashed with warm milk and a little butter for a soft, light side dish, with optional oven browning.

ingredients.name: peeled floury potatoes, cut into 3 cm chunks
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of russet potatoes; Yukon Gold gives a denser, creamier mash.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a dairy-free butter alternative.

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of lactose-free whole milk. Unsweetened plant milk changes the flavor.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Omit for an unsalted version; do not exchange different salts by volume.

steps: Cover {{potatoes}} with cold water and leave for 30 minutes, as in the source; then drain.

Put the potato pieces in a steamer over simmering water, keeping them above the water. Cover and steam for 20–25 minutes until a fork meets no resistance. Keep water in the lower pan as needed for steaming.
Warm {{milk}} in a small saucepan until steaming, without boiling. Transfer the tender potatoes to a warm bowl and mash by hand.
Mix {{butter}} and {{salt}} into the hot mash. Stir in half the warm milk, {{milk|0.5}}, followed by the remaining {{milk|0.5}}, until evenly combined. Avoid a blender or food processor.
Serve as six side portions. For the optional browned finish, place in a shallow oven-safe dish and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 10–15 minutes.
recipe.notes: The missing potato weight and salt amount are supplied as a modern formulation. Milk and butter are interpreted as 240 ml and 14 g. The original soak and steaming method are retained. Allow about 70 minutes without browning, or 85 with it. Yield and timing are planning estimates. This adaptation has not been kitchen-tested.
recipe.source: Canadian Farm Cook Book (1911), author not recorded. https://archive.org/details/canadianfarmcook00unse Modern adaptation by SavorShelf. Mashing technique cross-check: https://www.idahopotato.com/recipes/traditional-mashed-idaho-potatoes ; quantities and steaming method above are this source adaptation, not that recipe.

recipe.title: Scrambled Eggs
recipe.description: Eggs scrambled in butter with a small splash of milk form tender curds. The source’s generous pepper amount gives a pronounced peppery finish.

ingredients.name: large eggs
ingredients.substitution: Use pasteurized shell eggs in the same number if preferred. An egg-free replacement needs a separate formulation.

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.substitution: Use 30 ml water for a less creamy result, or the same volume of lactose-free milk.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit to taste; salt does not provide the structure here.

ingredients.name: ground black pepper
ingredients.substitution: Use less if desired; the original recipe is strongly peppered. White pepper has a different flavor.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a dairy-free butter alternative; flavor will differ.

steps: Whisk {{eggs}}, {{milk}}, {{salt}} and {{pepper}} in a bowl until evenly combined.
Melt {{butter}} in a large nonstick frying pan over medium-low heat; do not let it brown.
Pour in the egg mixture. Move a spatula slowly across the base and fold the setting curds over, cooking about 3–5 minutes until the eggs are set and no liquid egg remains.
Remove from the heat and divide into three portions. Serve immediately; the pan’s retained heat continues to firm the eggs.
recipe.notes: This adaptation keeps the six-egg formula, interprets the old milk and butter measures in metric, supplies weighed seasoning and a three-portion yield, and clarifies heat and doneness. Pan size and stove heat affect timing. Yield and timing are planning estimates. This adaptation has not been kitchen-tested.
recipe.source: Canadian Farm Cook Book (1911), author not recorded. https://archive.org/details/canadianfarmcook00unse Modern adaptation by SavorShelf. Technique cross-check: https://www.incredibleegg.org/recipe/basic-scrambled-eggs/ ; this retains the historical formula rather than the reference recipe’s proportions.

recipe.title: Perunalunta (Riced Potatoes)
recipe.description: Cooked potatoes are pressed through a ricer into a light mound and seasoned with salt; this dish contains no rice.

ingredients.name: peeled potatoes, cut into equal 3 cm pieces
ingredients.substitution: Use a similarly sized potato with the same texture: waxy for intact pieces; floury for ricing. Large whole potatoes need longer cooking.

ingredients.name: cooking water
ingredients.substitution: Use drinking water; stock changes the flavor and salt level. Rinsing water is separate and is discarded.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit if preferred. Different salts can be exchanged by weight, not necessarily by spoon volume.

steps: Prepare {{potatoes}}. Remove sprouts and damaged or green areas; discard extensively green potatoes. Use floury potatoes and rinse the cut pieces.
Place the potatoes in a saucepan with {{water}}. The water should cover them by about 1 cm; add enough cold water if the pan requires it.
Bring to a boil, then simmer gently until tender to the center: about 15–20 minutes for 3 cm pieces.
Drain and let steam escape for 2–3 minutes. While hot, press through a potato ricer into a serving dish. Sprinkle evenly with {{salt}} and serve without compacting the potato.
recipe.notes: A tenderness test replaces dependence on the source’s fixed boiling time. The riced presentation is retained without adding milk or butter. Quantities not stated by the source, equipment guidance, yield and timing are modern estimates. Not kitchen-tested.
recipe.source: Keittokirja = Cook Book (1928), author not recorded. https://archive.org/details/keittokirjacookb00wall SavorShelf measured adaptation. Technique reference: https://idahopotato.com/dr-potato/best-way-to-boil-idaho-potatoes

recipe.title: Brambory vařené (Boiled Potatoes)
recipe.description: Peeled potatoes receive the source’s cold soak, then simmer until tender and finish with salt and a covered rest.

ingredients.name: peeled potatoes, cut into equal 3 cm pieces
ingredients.substitution: Use a similarly sized potato with the same texture: waxy for intact pieces; floury for ricing. Large whole potatoes need longer cooking.

ingredients.name: cooking water
ingredients.substitution: Use drinking water; stock changes the flavor and salt level. Rinsing water is separate and is discarded.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit if preferred. Different salts can be exchanged by weight, not necessarily by spoon volume.

steps: Prepare {{potatoes}}. Remove sprouts and damaged or green areas; discard extensively green potatoes. Cover with separate cold rinsing water for 1 hour, then drain.
Bring {{water}} to a boil in a saucepan that holds the potatoes comfortably. Carefully add the potatoes; water should just cover them. If necessary, add enough hot water to cover.
Reduce to a gentle simmer. Cook about 20–25 minutes, until a thin knife enters the center without resistance. Do not use time alone as the test.
Drain carefully and return to the warm pan off the heat. Sprinkle with {{salt}} and gently shake. Cover and leave 5 minutes, as in the source.
recipe.notes: The hot-water start and source-specific preparation are retained. Choose a pan and water level that keep the pieces submerged. Quantities not stated by the source, equipment guidance, yield and timing are modern estimates. Not kitchen-tested.

recipe.title: Plain Rice to Serve with Curry
recipe.description: Basmati rice is boiled in salted water and drained for a plain, separate accompaniment to curry.

ingredients.name: dry white basmati rice
ingredients.substitution: Use another non-parboiled white long-grain rice and follow its doneness cues. Brown, parboiled and quick-cooking rice need different timings and liquid ratios.

ingredients.name: cooking water
ingredients.substitution: Use drinking water; stock changes the flavor and salt level. Rinsing water is separate and is discarded.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit if preferred. Different salts can be exchanged by weight, not necessarily by spoon volume.

steps: Rinse {{rice}} in a sieve under cold drinking water until the runoff is mostly clear.
Bring {{water}} and {{salt}} to a boil in a saucepan. Add the drained rice and return to a gentle boil.
Cook uncovered until the grains are tender but separate, checking from 10 minutes for basmati or 12 minutes for other long-grain white rice; allow up to 20 minutes if needed.
Drain in a fine sieve. Return to the warm pan off the heat for 3 minutes so excess moisture can evaporate. Gently loosen and serve separately from the main dish.
recipe.notes: Rice type, batch size, water and salt quantities are supplied as modern choices. The source’s excess-water method is retained; rice-package timing and actual tenderness take priority over a historical fixed time. Quantities not stated by the source, equipment guidance, yield and timing are modern estimates. Not kitchen-tested.
recipe.source: The Virginia Housewife; Or, Methodical Cook (1824), Mary Randolph. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/12519 SavorShelf measured adaptation. Technique reference: https://www.tilda.com/blog/quick-guides/how-to-cook-the-perfect-basmati-rice/

recipe.title: To Boil Rice — Modern Absorption Adaptation
recipe.description: White long-grain rice cooks in measured salted water and rests covered; this is a modern adaptation of the source’s boil-and-dry method.

ingredients.name: dry white basmati rice
ingredients.substitution: Use another non-parboiled white long-grain rice and follow its doneness cues. Brown, parboiled and quick-cooking rice need different timings and liquid ratios.

ingredients.name: cooking water
ingredients.substitution: Use drinking water; stock changes the flavor and salt level. Rinsing water is separate and is discarded.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit if preferred. Different salts can be exchanged by weight, not necessarily by spoon volume.

steps: Rinse {{rice}} in a sieve under cold drinking water until the runoff is mostly clear.
Combine the drained rice with {{water}} and {{salt}} in a small, heavy saucepan with a close-fitting lid. Bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce to the lowest heat and cook about 12–15 minutes until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender. If still firm and dry, add 15–30 ml hot water and cook a few minutes longer.
Remove from the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes, then separate the grains gently with a fork. Do not multiply cooking time when scaling; use a suitable pan.
recipe.notes: The source’s draining/coals stage is replaced with a measured absorption method and covered rest. The old cup ratio is not claimed as an exact modern conversion. Quantities not stated by the source, equipment guidance, yield and timing are modern estimates. Not kitchen-tested.
